   293	  if [ "$PRUNED" -gt 0 ]; then
   294	    GAP_PDF="$GAP_PDF; $PRUNED LaTeX build intermediate(s) pruned"
   295	    log "pruned $PRUNED LaTeX build intermediate(s)"
   296	  fi
   297	elif [ "$BUILD_PDF" -eq 1 ]; then
   298	  GAP_PDF="skipped: docs/paper-gaps/Makefile is not in this revision"
   299	  log "$GAP_PDF"
   300	fi
   301	
   302	# ---- 4. PDF text, so the leak scan is not blind to the binaries -----------
   303	
   304	# The leak scan reads the text-file list built in step 2, which by construction
   305	# skips binaries; a PDF -- one built just above, or one tracked in git -- would
   306	# otherwise ship without anything looking inside it.  Its text is extracted
   307	# here and appended to the same list, under a path that maps back to the
   308	# shipped file.  If it cannot be extracted the run stops: an unscanned binary
   309	# is exactly what the header promises cannot ship.
   310	PDF_TEXT_DIR="$WORK/pdf-text"
   311	PDF_LIST="$WORK/pdfs"
   312	find "$SNAP" -type f -name '*.pdf' > "$PDF_LIST"
   313	PDF_COUNT=$(wc -l < "$PDF_LIST" | tr -d ' ')
   314	PDF_SCAN="none in the snapshot"
   315	if [ "$PDF_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
   316	  command -v pdftotext >/dev/null 2>&1 || die \
   317	    "$PDF_COUNT PDF(s) in the snapshot but pdftotext (poppler-utils) is not installed; the leak scan cannot read them"
   318	  while IFS= read -r pdf; do
   319	    rel=${pdf#"$SNAP"/}
   320	    out="$PDF_TEXT_DIR/$rel.txt"
   321	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$out")"
   322	    pdftotext -q "$pdf" "$out" 2>/dev/null \
   323	      || die "cannot extract the text of $rel for the leak scan"
   324	    printf '%s\0' "$out" >> "$TEXT_LIST"
   325	  done < "$PDF_LIST"
   326	  PDF_SCAN="$PDF_COUNT PDF(s), text extracted with pdftotext and scanned"
   327	  log "$PDF_SCAN"
   328	fi
   329	
   330	# ---- 4b. the anonymization took, and is not taken on trust ----------------
   331	
   332	# `--anonymize` promises the reader of docs/ARTIFACT.md that the strings in
   333	# ANON_RULES are gone; nothing but this check makes the promise good, and a
   334	# silent miss is worse than no flag at all, because a submitter would ship on
   335	# it.  Every rule's literal text and its sed-regex-escaped spelling are looked
   336	# for as FIXED strings in everything the leak scan will read: the text files as
   337	# the pass left them, and the extracted text of every shipped PDF, which `sed`
   338	# cannot reach at all.  Checking the escaped spelling is load-bearing: that was
   339	# how the address survived in an earlier shipped allow-list entry.  The leak
   340	# patterns above would not catch these on their own — three of the five are
   341	# names, not address- or key-shaped.  A survivor stops the run, like a leak.
   342	if [ "$ANONYMIZE" -eq 1 ]; then
   343	  ANON_LEFT="$WORK/anon-left.txt"
   344	  : > "$ANON_LEFT"
   345	  for rule in "${ANON_RULES[@]}"; do
   346	    literal=${rule%% :: *}
   347	    escaped=$(sed_escape_pattern "$literal")
   348	    xargs -0 -r grep -HnF -e "$literal" < "$TEXT_LIST" >> "$ANON_LEFT" 2>/dev/null || true
   349	    if [ "$escaped" != "$literal" ]; then
   350	      xargs -0 -r grep -HnF -e "$escaped" < "$TEXT_LIST" >> "$ANON_LEFT" 2>/dev/null || true
   351	    fi
   352	  done
   353	  if [ -s "$ANON_LEFT" ]; then
   354	    # Same path mapping as the leak-scan report: snapshot-relative, and a PDF's
   355	    # extracted text named as the PDF that would have shipped.
   356	    sed -i -e "s|^$PDF_TEXT_DIR/\(.*\)\.txt:|\1 (text extracted from the PDF):|" \
   357	           -e "s|^$SNAP/||" "$ANON_LEFT"
   358	    echo "$PROG: ANONYMIZATION INCOMPLETE — the snapshot was not packaged." >&2
   359	    echo "$PROG: $(wc -l < "$ANON_LEFT" | tr -d ' ') surviving occurrence(s); first 40:" >&2
   360	    head -n 40 "$ANON_LEFT" >&2
   361	    echo "$PROG: a binary is the usual cause — rebuild it from the rewritten source, or drop it." >&2
   362	    exit 2
   363	  fi
   364	  log "anonymization check: no rule text survives in the snapshot"
   365	fi
   366	
   367	# ---- 5. measurements ------------------------------------------------------
   368	
   369	# Lean *code* lines: blank lines and lines lying wholly inside a line, block,

   114	        grouped.setdefault(entry.lean_decl, []).append(entry)
   115	    return grouped
   116	
   117	
   118	def _decl_has_any_leanok(entries: list[BlueprintEntry]) -> bool:
   119	    return any(_entry_has_leanok(entry) for entry in entries)
   120	
   121	
   122	def _decl_leanok_placement(entries: list[BlueprintEntry]) -> str:
   123	    """Classify a declaration's strongest ``\\leanok`` claim across ``entries``.
   124	
   125	    Following ``docs/blueprint_style_guide.md``:
   126	
   127	    * ``proof`` — at least one entry carries proof-level ``\\leanok``. This
   128	      is the only placement that claims the Lean proof is complete, so the
   129	      axiom-closure check *must* fail on ``sorryAx`` for these decls.
   130	    * ``statement`` — at least one entry carries statement-level
   131	      ``\\leanok`` but none carries proof-level. The Lean declaration
   132	      exists and its statement matches; the proof is not claimed complete,
   133	      so a ``sorryAx`` finding is reported as a warning rather than a
   134	      hard error.
   135	    * ``none`` — no ``\\leanok`` anywhere.
   136	    """
   137	    has_proof = any(entry.proof_has_leanok for entry in entries)
   138	    if has_proof:
   139	        return "proof"
   140	    has_statement = any(entry.has_leanok for entry in entries)
   141	    if has_statement:
   142	        return "statement"
   143	    return "none"
   144	
   145	
   146	def module_name_from_decl(decl: LeanDecl) -> str:
   147	    """Turn ``MIPStarRE/Foo/Bar.lean`` into ``MIPStarRE.Foo.Bar``."""
   148	    return ".".join(Path(decl.file).with_suffix("").parts)
   149	
   150	
   151	def group_decls_by_module(
   152	    decls: list[str],
   153	    lean_decls: dict[str, LeanDecl],
   154	) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
   155	    grouped: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   156	    for decl in decls:
   157	        if decl not in lean_decls:
   158	            continue
   159	        grouped[module_name_from_decl(lean_decls[decl])].append(decl)
   160	    return dict(sorted(grouped.items()))
   161	
   162	
   163	def parse_axiom_output(
   164	    output: str,
   165	    decls: list[str],
   166	    *,
   167	    harness_path: Path,
   168	    line_to_decl: dict[int, str],
   169	    returncode: int,
   170	) -> dict[str, DeclAxiomInfo] | None:
   171	    """Parse the output of a ``#print axioms`` harness.
   172	
   173	    Returns ``None`` when the harness failed before any declaration-specific
   174	    output could be attributed, typically because the imported module itself
   175	    failed to compile.
   176	    """
   177	    harness_str = str(harness_path)
   178	    loc_exact_re = re.compile(rf"^{re.escape(harness_str)}:(\d+):\d+:\s*(.*)$")
   179	
   180	    # Lean wraps subject names in matched quotes.  Allow apostrophes inside the
   181	    # name (Lean primes like `foo'` are common) by requiring the closing quote
   182	    # to match the opening one rather than treating `` ` `` and `'` as
   183	    # interchangeable terminators.
   184	    subject_re = re.compile(
   185	        r"^(?:`(?P<btick>[^`]+)`|'(?P<apos>.+)')\s+"
   186	        r"(depends on axioms:|does not depend on any axioms)"
   187	    )
   188	    decl_set = set(decls)
   189	
   190	    records: dict[str, list[str]] = {decl: [] for decl in decls}
   191	    current: str | None = None
   192	    for raw_line in output.splitlines():
   193	        content = raw_line
   194	        matched: str | None = None
   195	
   196	        subject = subject_re.match(raw_line)
   197	        if subject:
   198	            name = subject.group("btick") or subject.group("apos")
   199	            if name in decl_set:
   200	                matched = name
   201	
   202	        if matched is None:
   203	            match = loc_exact_re.match(raw_line)
   204	            if match:
   205	                line_no = int(match.group(1))
   206	                if line_no in line_to_decl:
   207	                    matched = line_to_decl[line_no]
   208	                    content = match.group(2)
   209	
   210	        if matched is not None:
   211	            current = matched
   212	        if current is not None:
   213	            records[current].append(content)
   214	
   215	    if returncode != 0 and not any(records.values()):
   216	        return None
   217	
   218	    unknown_re = re.compile(r"unknown\s+(identifier|constant)")
   219	    depends_re = re.compile(r"depends on axioms:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]", re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
   220	
   221	    parsed: dict[str, DeclAxiomInfo] = {}
   222	    for decl in decls:
   223	        joined = "\n".join(records.get(decl, []))
   224	        joined_lc = joined.lower()
   225	        exists = True
   226	        axioms: list[str] = []
   227	        parse_error = False
   228	        if not joined:
   229	            exists = False
   230	        elif unknown_re.search(joined_lc):
   231	            exists = False
   232	        elif "does not depend on any axioms" in joined_lc:
   233	            pass
   234	        else:
   235	            match = depends_re.search(joined)
   236	            if match:
   237	                axioms = [piece.strip() for piece in match.group(1).split(",") if piece.strip()]
   238	            else:
   239	                parse_error = True
   240	        parsed[decl] = DeclAxiomInfo(
   241	            exists=exists,
   242	            axioms=axioms,
   243	            raw=joined,
   244	            parse_error=parse_error,
   245	        )
   246	    return parsed
   247	
   248	
   249	def module_source_path(repo_root: Path, module: str) -> Path:
   250	    """Return the local source path for a repository module."""
   251	    return repo_root / Path(*module.split(".")).with_suffix(".lean")
   252	
   253	
   254	def module_output_paths(repo_root: Path, module: str) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
   255	    """Return the expected ``.olean`` / ``.ilean`` output paths."""
   256	    rel = Path(*module.split("."))
   257	    olean = repo_root / ".lake" / "build" / "lib" / "lean" / rel.with_suffix(".olean")
   258	    ilean = repo_root / ".lake" / "build" / "lib" / "lean" / rel.with_suffix(".ilean")
   259	    return olean, ilean
   260	
   261	
   262	def ensure_module_olean(repo_root: Path, module: str, lake: str) -> str | None:
   263	    """Build a local module on demand when its ``.olean`` is missing.
   264	
   265	    This is a fallback used when ``lake build`` has not been run beforehand.
   266	    It only emits the ``.olean`` / ``.ilean`` artifacts the axiom harness
   267	    needs — no C output — since generating C adds significant overhead
   268	    without providing any value to ``#print axioms``.
   269	    """
   270	    source = module_source_path(repo_root, module)
   271	    if not source.is_file():
   272	        return None
   273	
   274	    olean, ilean = module_output_paths(repo_root, module)
   275	    if olean.exists():
   276	        return None
   277	
   278	    olean.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   279	    ilean.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   280	
   281	    proc = subprocess.run(
   282	        [
   283	            lake,
   284	            "env",
   285	            "lean",
   286	            str(source.relative_to(repo_root)),
   287	            "-o",
   288	            str(olean),
   289	            "-i",
   290	            str(ilean),
   291	        ],
   292	        cwd=repo_root,
   293	        capture_output=True,
   294	        text=True,
   295	    )
   296	    if proc.returncode == 0:
   297	        return None
   298	    output = _strip_ansi((proc.stdout or "") + "\n" + (proc.stderr or "")).strip()
   299	    tail = "\n".join(output.splitlines()[-10:]).strip()
   300	    return (
   301	        f"could not build missing object file for {module}."
   302	        + (f" Lean output tail: {tail}" if tail else "")
   303	    )
   304	
   305	
   306	def run_axiom_batch(
   307	    imports: list[str],
   308	    decls: list[str],
   309	    *,
   310	    repo_root: Path,
   311	    lake: str,
   312	) -> tuple[dict[str, DeclAxiomInfo] | None, str]:
   313	    """Run one temporary Lean harness for a batch of declarations."""
   314	    for module in imports:
   315	        build_error = ensure_module_olean(repo_root, module, lake)
   316	        if build_error is not None:
   317	            return None, build_error
   318	
   319	    header = [f"import {module}" for module in imports] + [""]
   320	    body = [f"#print axioms {decl}" for decl in decls]
   321	    first_body_line = len(header) + 1
   322	    line_to_decl = {first_body_line + idx: decl for idx, decl in enumerate(decls)}
   323	
   324	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
   325	        harness = Path(temp_dir) / "BlueprintLeanokAxioms.lean"
   326	        harness.write_text("\n".join(header + body) + "\n")
   327	        proc = subprocess.run(
   328	            [lake, "env", "lean", str(harness)],
   329	            cwd=repo_root,
   330	            capture_output=True,
   331	            text=True,
   332	        )
   333	        harness_path = harness
   334	
   335	    output = _strip_ansi((proc.stdout or "") + "\n" + (proc.stderr or "")).strip()
   336	    parsed = parse_axiom_output(
   337	        output,
   338	        decls,
   339	        harness_path=harness_path,
   340	        line_to_decl=line_to_decl,
   341	        returncode=proc.returncode,
   342	    )
   343	    return parsed, output
   344	
   345	
   346	def _run_decl_axiom_checks_items(
   347	    items: list[tuple[str, list[str]]],
   348	    *,
   349	    repo_root: Path,
   350	    lake: str,
   351	    depth: int = 0,
   352	) -> dict[str, DeclAxiomInfo]:
   353	    """Run ``#print axioms`` on one batch of module imports, splitting on failure."""
   354	    if not items:
   355	        return {}
   356	
   357	    imports = [module for module, _ in items]
   358	    decls = [decl for _, module_decls in items for decl in module_decls]
   359	    indent = "  " * (depth + 1)
   360	    print(
   361	        f"{indent}Checking batch: {len(decls)} decl(s) across {len(items)} module(s) …"
   362	    )
   363	    parsed, output = run_axiom_batch(
   364	        imports,
   365	        decls,
   366	        repo_root=repo_root,
   367	        lake=lake,
   368	    )
   369	    if parsed is not None:
   370	        print(f"{indent}Batch succeeded.")
   371	        return parsed
   372	
   373	    if len(items) == 1:
   374	        module, module_decls = items[0]
   375	        tail = "\n".join(output.splitlines()[-10:]).strip()
   376	        reason = (
   377	            f"could not run `#print axioms` after importing {module}."
   378	            + (f" Lean output tail: {tail}" if tail else "")
   379	        )
   380	        print(f"{indent}Batch failed at module {module}.")
   381	        return {
   382	            decl: DeclAxiomInfo(
   383	                exists=True,
   384	                raw=output,
   385	                parse_error=True,
   386	                harness_error=reason,
   387	            )
   388	            for decl in module_decls
   389	        }
   390	
   391	    mid = len(items) // 2
   392	    print(
   393	        f"{indent}Batch failed before declaration output; splitting into "
   394	        f"{mid} and {len(items) - mid} module(s)."
   395	    )
   396	    left = _run_decl_axiom_checks_items(
   397	        items[:mid],
   398	        repo_root=repo_root,
   399	        lake=lake,
   400	        depth=depth + 1,
   401	    )
   402	    right = _run_decl_axiom_checks_items(
   403	        items[mid:],
   404	        repo_root=repo_root,
   405	        lake=lake,
   406	        depth=depth + 1,
   407	    )
   408	    left.update(right)
   409	    return left
   410	
   411	
   412	def run_decl_axiom_checks(
   413	    decls: list[str],
   414	    *,
   415	    lean_decls: dict[str, LeanDecl],
   416	    repo_root: Path,
   417	    lake: str,
   418	) -> dict[str, DeclAxiomInfo]:
   419	    """Run ``#print axioms`` on the given declarations, grouped by module."""
   420	    grouped = group_decls_by_module(decls, lean_decls)

## 5. Review Checklist

Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:

1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.
   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.

2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and
   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`
   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.

3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration
   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from
   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See
   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local
   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag
   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical
   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,
   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file
   under [audits/](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/tree/main/audits).
   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and
   format in
   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/blob/main/audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).
   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   public name.
   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/tree/main/audits)
   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or
   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or
   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.

4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask
   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See
   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow
   exception policy.

5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved
   metavariables.

6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on
   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.

7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be
   upstreamed to Mathlib?

8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.
   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the
   relevant arXiv paper(s).

9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement
   from the blueprint, add `\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\leanok` tags to the
   corresponding `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file. If the PR adds a public
   auxiliary lemma that is not a named statement in the original paper, record
   that explicitly: the Lean docstring should call it a formalization-only
   auxiliary lemma and the blueprint should either omit it as private/internal
   infrastructure or include it as a clearly subordinate support node connected
   by `\uses{...}`. See
   [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md#recording-formalization-only-lemmas).
   PR descriptions and follow-up issues should cite the corresponding paper or
   blueprint path, line, label, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.
   Reviewers should also check for early drift from the source: new hypotheses,
   weakened conclusions, changed quantifier order, altered error parameters,
   or renamed obligation structures that turn a paper theorem into a conditional
   theorem.  If such drift appears, request a statement integrity audit before
   reviewing the proof.  A bridge or residual hypothesis should be treated as
   proof debt to remove, not as evidence that the paper statement has been
   formalized.

10. **Scaffolding integrity** -- If the PR introduces or modifies scaffolded
   definitions (types, theorem statements with `sorry` proofs), verify that
   the types and API surface align with Mathlib. Scaffolding that uses custom
   types incompatible with Mathlib blocks future proof work. See
   the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and
   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) for details.

11. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** -- Review against
   [anti_patterns.md](anti_patterns.md), which catalogues subtler failure
   modes that pass the proof-integrity blocker checks but still fail
   to prove the claimed mathematics: conclusion-shaped hypotheses (A1),
   `:= rfl` definitional sleight-of-hand (A2), zero-fallback branches
   hiding preconditions (A3), trivial default witnesses (A4),
   Mathlib-bypass castles (A5), and external `*Statement` smuggles (A6).
   Use the reviewer checklist at the end of that file.

12. **Proof frontier integrity** -- If the PR introduces or threads structure
   fields such as `*Input`, `*Residual`, `*BridgeInputs`, `*Witness`,
   `*Statement`, `*Conclusion`, or `*Package`, review it against
   [proof_frontier_review.md](proof_frontier_review.md). A PR that only
   repackages an assumption should not be described as proving the corresponding
   paper step; it must name the missing obligation discharger or link the native
   sub-issue that tracks it.  For source-labelled theorems, the preferred repair
   is to extract any usable proof content into source-faithful lemmas and
   restore the paper-aligned statement, even if the remaining proof is a tracked
   `sorry` during the cleanup.  For source-labelled proof gaps, also use the
   protocol in
   [paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex).

### Semantic scaffold checklist (required for core math objects)

For semantic objects such as measurements, submeasurements, distributions,
averaged operators, and packaged theorem outputs, reviewers should additionally
verify:

1. **Impossible states check** -- Does the structure exclude states that are
   impossible under the paper definition?
2. **Derived-field check** -- If a field is mathematically derived
   (e.g. `total = ∑ a, outcome a`), is it either derived on demand or stored
   together with an equality proof (e.g. `sum_eq_total`)?
3. **Invariant bundling check** -- Are core invariants (positivity,
   boundedness/normalization, completeness where applicable) encoded directly
   in the structure or constructor, rather than deferred to downstream lemmas?
4. **Stress-test check** -- Is at least one nontrivial theorem in scope of the
   PR provable/stated against the scaffold without adding ad hoc assumptions?

If any answer is "no", treat the scaffold as unsafe and request a follow-up
before broad theorem layering continues.

     1	# Deviations from the source paper
     2	
     3	This page lists every recorded place where the Lean development in this
     4	repository differs from its source paper, *MIP\* = RE* (arXiv:2001.04383),
     5	whose TeX is mirrored under `references/qpbt-paper/`. It is written for a
     6	reviewer who wants to know, before reading any Lean, what was changed and why.
     7	
     8	The short answer: the formalization corrects false printed claims, makes
     9	implicit source-domain conditions explicit as faithful boundary hypotheses,
    10	records unestablished printed claims without asserting them, and documents
    11	statement-preserving alternative proofs and representations. **No headline
    12	theorem depends on an unproved claim.** Section
    13	[No headline theorem rests on an unproved claim](#no-headline-theorem-rests-on-an-unproved-claim)
    14	says how to check that mechanically.
    15	
    16	Detail for each row lives in a mathematical note under `docs/paper-gaps/`. The
    17	machine-readable index of those notes is
    18	[`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md`](paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md), which

    31	
    32	**Printed-claim status** is the single most important column. It answers: what
    33	happened to the sentence as the paper prints it?
    34	
    35	| Status | Meaning |
    36	|---|---|

# ---- 7. internal Markdown links -------------------------------------------

# A page that ships must not point at a page that does not.  The `docs/`
# carve-out is what makes this possible: a shipped page may link a workflow-only
# page the allow-list drops.  This is a report, not a gate -- a link may
# legitimately be waiting for a page another packet adds -- but it is recorded
# in the MANIFEST so that nobody has to discover it by clicking.
DEAD_LINKS=$(python3 - "$SNAP" <<'PY' || echo "check failed"
import os, re, sys

root = sys.argv[1]
link = re.compile(r"\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)\s]+)")
dead = total = 0
report = []
for base, _dirs, names in os.walk(root):
    for name in names:
        if not name.endswith(".md"):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(base, name)
        try:
            text = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
        except OSError:
            continue
        for match in link.finditer(text):
            target = match.group(1).split("#")[0].strip()
            if not target or "://" in target or target.startswith("mailto:"):
                continue
            total += 1
            if not os.path.exists(os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, target))):
                dead += 1
                report.append("%s -> %s" % (os.path.relpath(path, root), target))
print("%d dead of %d checked" % (dead, total))
for line in sorted(set(report)):
    print("  dead link: " + line, file=sys.stderr)
PY
)
log "internal Markdown links: $DEAD_LINKS"

# ---- 7b. paper locators ---------------------------------------------------

# Now that the paper sources ship, a docstring's `references/<paper>/<file>.tex`
# locator is a path a reviewer can open in the snapshot — so a locator naming a
# file that is not there is worth saying out loud.  A report, not a gate: the
# locator may name a section the mirror splits differently, and a packaging
# script is the wrong place to decide that.  The MANIFEST carries the count so
# that it cannot rot unnoticed.
# The mirrors' file names are lower case throughout, so a locator whose file
# component carries a capital is a fill-in placeholder rather than a citation --
# `references/ldt-paper/FILE.tex` in the gap-note template and the row for it in
# the gap-note README.  Those are dropped here instead of being reported as
# absent every time.
LOC_LIST="$WORK/paper-locators"
grep -rhoE 'references/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.tex' \
    "$SNAP/MIPStarRE" "$SNAP/blueprint/src" "$SNAP/docs" 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -vE '/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\.tex$' \
  | sort -u > "$LOC_LIST" || true
LOC_TOTAL=$(wc -l < "$LOC_LIST" | tr -d ' ')
LOC_DEAD_LIST=$(while read -r locator; do
    [ -f "$SNAP/$locator" ] || printf '%s ' "$locator"
  done < "$LOC_LIST")
LOC_DEAD=$(printf '%s' "$LOC_DEAD_LIST" | wc -w | tr -d ' ')
if [ "$LOC_DEAD" -gt 0 ]; then
  PAPER_LOCATORS="$LOC_DEAD of $LOC_TOTAL cited files absent: $LOC_DEAD_LIST"

  PAPER_LOCATORS="all $LOC_TOTAL cited files are in the snapshot"

KEPT_HITS="$WORK/leaks-kept.txt"

  grep -vE "$1" "$KEPT_HITS" > "$KEPT_HITS.next" 2>/dev/null || true

drop_exact_finding() {
  awk -F: -v path="$1" -v text="$2" \
    'NF == 3 && $1 == path && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $3 == text { next } { print }' \
    "$KEPT_HITS" > "$KEPT_HITS.next"
  mv "$KEPT_HITS.next" "$KEPT_HITS"
}
for entry in "${LEAK_ALLOW[@]}"; do
  drop_forgiven ":[0-9]+:.*(${entry%% :: *})"
done
for entry in "${LEAK_ALLOW_IN[@]}"; do
  rest=${entry#* :: }
  drop_forgiven "(${entry%% :: *})[^:]*:[0-9]+:.*(${rest%% :: *})"
done

KEPT=$(wc -l < "$KEPT_HITS" | tr -d ' ')
log "leak scan: $RAW raw hit(s), $(( RAW - KEPT )) allow-listed, $KEPT remaining"

if [ -s "$KEPT_HITS" ]; then
  echo "$PROG: LEAK SCAN FAILED — the snapshot was not packaged." >&2
  echo "$PROG: $KEPT hit(s); first 40, paths relative to the snapshot:" >&2

  exit 2
fi
log "leak scan clean"

cp "$MANIFEST" "$OUT_DIR/$NAME.MANIFEST.txt"
if [ "$KEEP_TREE" -eq 1 ]; then

     1	# Comparator challenge generation
     2	
     3	This directory generates the self-contained statement files `Challenge.lean`
     4	used by companion repositories — for the low individual degree test,
     5	[LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator), and for the quantum
     6	Pauli basis test,
     7	[QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator) — to verify,
     8	with the official
     9	[leanprover/comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator), that this
    10	library proves the target theorems.  Background and trust model:
    11	`docs/comparator.md`.
    12	
    13	A generated challenge imports only Mathlib and, when split, its own mirror
    14	modules.  It re-declares, verbatim and in dependency order, every declaration
    15	in the kernel closure of its target statements, each with a provenance comment;
    16	the targets themselves are stated with `sorry`.
    17	
    18	## Challenges
    19	
    20	Each challenge is one configuration file under `challenges/`:
    21	
    22	| file | targets | expected copy | challenge repository |
    23	|---|---|---|---|
    24	| `challenges/ldt.json` | `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` | `expected/Challenge.lean.expected` | [LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator) |
    25	| `challenges/qpbt.json` | four QPBT headline theorems | `expected/qpbt/` (one module per library module) | [QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator) |
    26	
    27	The four QPBT targets are `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one`,
    28	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`, and
    29	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.
    30	
    31	A configuration names the Lean modules the extractor imports, the target
    32	theorems whose statement closure it takes, the header and footer files wrapped
    33	around the assembled body, the checked-in expected copy, and the per-challenge
    34	elaboration-context tables (`extras`, `module_preludes`).  The schema, with the
    35	meaning of every key, is documented at the top of `challenge_config.py`; unknown
    36	keys are rejected, so a typo fails loudly rather than silently dropping context.
    37	
    38	`require_expected` distinguishes a challenge that must stay regenerated (`true`,
    39	a missing expected copy is an error) from one still being developed (`false`,
    40	a missing expected copy is reported and skipped).
    41	
    42	Adding a challenge means adding a configuration file, a header and a footer —
    43	no generator code changes and, for the machine-wide guard in `local/bin/ci.sh`,
    44	no CI change either, because that guard passes no `--challenge` and therefore
    45	checks every configuration it finds.
    46	
    47	## Drift guard and regeneration
    48	
    49	The repository keeps each generated challenge checked in under `expected/`.
    50	The LDT copy has a final `.expected` suffix, which keeps that intentionally
    51	monolithic fixture out of the 1000-line project-source guard; the QPBT copy is
    52	a split directory. The PR CI guard regenerates every configured challenge in a
    53	temporary directory and byte-compares it with the checked-in file or tree; it
    54	never writes `Challenge.lean` at the repository root.
    55	
    56	Run the deterministic guard from the repository root (requires a built
    57	library).  With no `--challenge` every configured challenge is checked:
    58	
    59	```sh
    60	python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root .
    61	python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --challenge qpbt
    62	```
    63	
    64	Add `--challenge <name>` (repeatable) to restrict the run to one challenge.
    65	
    66	To update a checked-in expected copy after an intentional statement or
    67	dependency change, run the exact maintenance command:
    68	
    69	```sh
    70	python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --update
    71	```
    72	
    73	That command refuses a challenge whose configured header or footer file is not
    74	in the tree, and reports it as an error while still updating the others: the
    75	copy it would write omits those statements, and once such a copy exists the
    76	`require_expected: false` skip no longer applies, so every later drift run
    77	would report a challenge that states nothing as current.
    78	
    79	The regeneration guard and the LDT preservation regression answer different
    80	questions.  Regeneration checks that the fixture agrees with the current
    81	library.  `ComparatorChallengeDriftTests.test_ldt_expected_matches_original_baseline`
    82	also hashes `expected/Challenge.lean.expected` and requires the original LDT
    83	digest
    84	`cbe5642bb88db75f86bd79936896e684aa407a02108d8259ead71a0738783e73`.
    85	Consequently, a QPBT-only change cannot silently update both the library and the
    86	generated LDT fixture.
    87	
    88	For an intentional future LDT change, first regenerate from fresh built
    89	metadata, audit the exact fixture diff, and verify it in LDT-comparator.  Then
    90	update `LDT_BASELINE_SHA256` in
    91	`scripts/tests/test_comparator_challenge_drift.py` explicitly in the same
    92	reviewed change, with the mathematical reason for changing the LDT closure.
    93	
    94	To generate a challenge somewhere else without touching the checked-in copy —
    95	the usual loop while filling in a new challenge's context tables:
    96	
    97	```sh
    98	python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . \
    99	    --challenge qpbt --write /tmp/Challenge.lean
   100	```
   101	
   102	The update command performs the extraction and assembly pipeline below in a
   103	temporary directory; the same steps run by hand, shown here for the QPBT
   104	challenge, reproduce the same file:
   105	
   106	```sh
   107	# 1. render the extractor with this challenge's own import block.  A Lean module
   108	#    header cannot be computed at elaboration time, so the checked-in
   109	#    extract_closure.lean carries the LDT import block and every consumer
   110	#    substitutes the challenge's `imports` into a copy of it; run unrendered on
   111	#    a QPBT target it fails with "target not found", because no LDT module
   112	#    imports QPBT.
   113	python3 - <<'PY' > extract_closure_qpbt.lean
   114	import sys
   115	sys.path.insert(0, "scripts/comparator")
   116	from challenge_config import load_challenges
   117	from check_challenge_drift import EXTRACTOR, render_extractor
   118	(challenge,) = load_challenges(["qpbt"])
   119	sys.stdout.write(render_extractor(challenge, EXTRACTOR.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
   120	PY
   121	
   122	# 2. extract the closure of the challenge's target statements (a Lean
   123	#    metaprogram mirroring comparator's runForUsedConsts traversal).  The
   124	#    targets reach the extractor in MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS; with that
   125	#    variable unset it closes the LDT main theorem:
   126	MIPSTARRE_COMPARATOR_TARGETS="MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness,MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit,MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one,MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness" \
   127	  lake env lean extract_closure_qpbt.lean > closure.tsv
   128	awk -F'\t' 'NF==4' closure.tsv > closure.clean.tsv
   129	
   130	# 3. assemble the challenge body (topological order, namespace handling)
   131	# `qpbt` is split, so the assembler writes a directory:
   132	python3 scripts/comparator/assemble_challenge.py closure.clean.tsv \
   133	    --challenge qpbt --split-dir scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt
   134	```
   135	
   136	For the LDT challenge step 1 is a no-op — the checked-in extractor already
   137	carries that challenge's import block — so `lake env lean
   138	scripts/comparator/extract_closure.lean` with no environment variable set is
   139	step 2 of the LDT pipeline as it stands.
   140	
   141	Then copy the expected file, or the QPBT `Challenge.lean` and `Challenge/`
   142	tree, into the matching comparator repository. Bump the `rev` pin in its
   143	`lakefile.toml` and `lake-manifest.json` to the library commit from which it was
   144	generated, and run its `./verify.sh` (its CI also runs on every push).
   145	
   146	Comparator verification status is maintained in `docs/comparator.md`, including
   147	the exact four-target run, merged-main library pin, real-landrun and nanoda
   148	evidence, and trust qualifications.  This operational README documents
   149	generation and deliberately does not duplicate mutable acceptance status.
   150	
   151	## Maintenance notes
   152	
   153	- A challenge's `extras`/`module_preludes` tables carry elaboration context
   154	  (attribute commands, `CoeFun` instances, `variable`/`open` blocks) that the
   155	  kernel closure cannot see.  Extend them if regeneration produces compile
   156	  errors in that challenge's `Challenge.lean`; the assembler fails loudly if one
   157	  of the challenge's own table keys no longer matches any extracted
   158	  declaration.  The tables are per challenge, so an LDT key never constrains the
   159	  QPBT closure or the other way round.
   160	- A `module_preludes` entry is one scope, or a list of scopes each covering a
   161	  line range (`first`/`last`) of its module: a module needs one scope per source
   162	  section whose context differs.  A scope opened with `noncomputable section` in
   163	  the source is marked `"noncomputable": true`, because the definitions inside
   164	  such a section carry no `noncomputable` keyword of their own.
   165	- The target statements in each footer mirror the theorems in the library:
   166	  `challenge_footer.lean` mirrors
   167	  `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean`, and
   168	  `challenge_qpbt_footer.lean` mirrors
   169	  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Completeness.lean`,
   170	  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean`,
   171	  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean`, and
   172	  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/QubitForm.lean`.  If a library statement changes, update
   173	  the footer too - comparator fails with "theorem statement do not match" until
   174	  the two agree.
   175	- Declarations without a source range (compiler-generated congruence lemmas
   176	  and `autoParam` helpers) are emitted as explanatory comments; they
   177	  regenerate identically during elaboration of the challenge file.
   178	- A configured header or footer file that is not in the tree is reported and
   179	  omitted, so a challenge under development can be generated before its footer
   180	  exists.  That omission is confined to `--write`: `--update` refuses such a
   181	  challenge rather than checking in a copy without that part.
   182	- A closure declaration cannot be `private`: a private name is qualified by its
   183	  defining module, so the challenge file could never re-declare it under the
   184	  library's name.  Closure members found to be private are made public in the
   185	  library (see `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment").
   186	
   187	
   188	## Split (multi-module) challenges
   189	
   190	A challenge whose JSON configuration sets `"split": true` is generated as one
   191	Mathlib-only module per contributing library module instead of one file:
   192	
   193	```
   194	python3 scripts/comparator/assemble_challenge.py <closure.tsv> \
   195	    --root . --challenge qpbt --split-dir <out>
   196	```
   197	
   198	`<out>/Challenge.lean` imports the parts under `<out>/Challenge/<library
   199	path>.lean` and carries the header and the `sorry`-ed target statements; each
   200	part imports Mathlib plus the mirrors of the library modules its source module
   201	imports.  The layout is what makes Lean generate the same auxiliary
   202	declarations, under the same names, as the library — see the "environment
   203	alignment" section of `docs/comparator.md`.  The checked-in copy is a
   204	directory, and `check_challenge_drift.py --challenge <name> [--update]`
   205	compares or rewrites the whole tree.

"""Regression tests for scripts/audit_blueprint_high_risk_links.py."""

from __future__ import annotations

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPT_DIR))

from audit_blueprint_high_risk_links import run_audit  # noqa: E402


def write_minimal_tree(root: Path, *, tex: str, axiom_audit: str) -> None:
    """Write the minimal files needed by the blueprint high-risk audit."""
    chapter = root / "blueprint" / "src" / "chapter"
    chapter.mkdir(parents=True)
    (chapter / "ch_test.tex").write_text(tex, encoding="utf-8")

    audit_dir = root / "MIPStarRE" / "LDT" / "Test"
    audit_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    (audit_dir / "AxiomAudit.lean").write_text(axiom_audit, encoding="utf-8")


class BlueprintHighRiskLinkAuditTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_high_risk_link_passes_when_decl_is_asserted(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            write_minimal_tree(
                root,
                tex=r"""
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:repair}
\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.RepairThing}
\leanok
This is a test statement.
\end{lemma}
""",
                axiom_audit="""
assert_no_sorry_axiom MIPStarRE.LDT.RepairThing
""",
            )

            result = run_audit(root)

        self.assertTrue(result.ok)
        self.assertEqual(result.scanned_entries, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.high_risk_entries, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.findings, ())

    def test_high_risk_link_passes_for_nested_assertion_in_namespace(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            write_minimal_tree(
                root,
                tex=r"""
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:slackness}
\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.SelfImprovement.PairWithSlackness.toStatementWithSlackness}
\leanok
This is a test statement.
\end{lemma}
""",
                axiom_audit="""
namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.SelfImprovement

assert_no_sorry_axiom PairWithSlackness.toStatementWithSlackness

end MIPStarRE.LDT.SelfImprovement
""",
            )

            result = run_audit(root)

        self.assertTrue(result.ok)
        self.assertEqual(result.scanned_entries, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.high_risk_entries, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.findings, ())

    def test_high_risk_link_fails_without_axiom_audit_assertion(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            write_minimal_tree(
                root,
                tex=r"""
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:bridge}
\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.MainBridgeHypotheses}
This is a test statement.
\end{proposition}
""",
                axiom_audit="",
            )

            result = run_audit(root)

        self.assertFalse(result.ok)
        self.assertEqual(result.high_risk_entries, 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(result.findings), 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.findings[0].decl, "MIPStarRE.LDT.MainBridgeHypotheses")
        self.assertEqual(result.findings[0].label, "prop:bridge")

    def test_non_high_risk_link_is_ignored(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            write_minimal_tree(
                root,
                tex=r"""
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:ordinary}
\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.ordinaryTheorem}
\leanok
This is a test statement.
\end{theorem}
""",
                axiom_audit="",
            )

            result = run_audit(root)

        self.assertTrue(result.ok)
        self.assertEqual(result.scanned_entries, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.high_risk_entries, 0)

    def test_statement_named_link_requires_axiom_audit_assertion(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root = Path(tmp)
            write_minimal_tree(
                root,
                tex=r"""
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:statement}
\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.SomeStatement}
This is a test statement.
\end{lemma}
""",
                axiom_audit="",
            )

            result = run_audit(root)

        self.assertFalse(result.ok)
        self.assertEqual(result.high_risk_entries, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.findings[0].decl, "MIPStarRE.LDT.SomeStatement")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

from pathlib import Path

)


class BlueprintAxiomAuditNeededTests(unittest.TestCase):

        diff = r"""
diff --git a/blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex b/blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex
@@ -10,0 +11 @@
+  \uses{lem:looks-easy-but-took-me-a-while}
"""
        self.assertFalse(diff_touches_formalization_markers(diff))
        self.assertFalse(
            needs_axiom_audit_for_paths(["blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex"], diff)
        )

    def test_lean_marker_blueprint_diff_requires_heavy_audit(self) -> None:
        diff = r"""
diff --git a/blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex b/blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex
@@ -10,0 +11,2 @@
+  \lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Pasting.someTheorem}
+  \leanok
"""
        self.assertTrue(diff_touches_formalization_markers(diff))
        self.assertTrue(
            needs_axiom_audit_for_paths(["blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex"], diff)
        )

    def test_removed_leanok_requires_heavy_audit(self) -> None:
        diff = r"""
diff --git a/blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex b/blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex
@@ -10 +9,0 @@
-  \leanok
"""
        self.assertTrue(diff_touches_formalization_markers(diff))

    def test_lean_source_requires_heavy_audit(self) -> None:
        self.assertTrue(
            needs_axiom_audit_for_paths(["MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean"])
        )

    def test_workflow_or_audit_script_change_requires_heavy_audit(self) -> None:
        self.assertTrue(needs_axiom_audit_for_paths([".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml"]))
        self.assertTrue(needs_axiom_audit_for_paths(["scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py"]))

    def test_plain_blueprint_prose_skips_heavy_audit(self) -> None:
        diff = r"""
diff --git a/blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex b/blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex
@@ -10 +10 @@
-  Old prose.
+  New prose.
"""
        self.assertFalse(
            needs_axiom_audit_for_paths(["blueprint/src/chapter/ch09_pasting.tex"], diff)
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

class BlueprintLeanokAxiomsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_parse_axiom_output_classifies_sorry_and_missing_decls(self) -> None:
        harness = Path("/tmp/BlueprintLeanokAxioms.lean")
        output = "\n".join(
            [
                "'Foo.good' does not depend on any axioms",
                "'Foo.bad' depends on axioms: [Classical.choice, sorryAx]",
                f"{harness}:5:0: error: unknown constant 'Foo.missing'",
            ]
        )
        results = parse_axiom_output(
            output,
            ["Foo.good", "Foo.bad", "Foo.missing"],
            harness_path=harness,
            line_to_decl={3: "Foo.good", 4: "Foo.bad", 5: "Foo.missing"},
            returncode=1,
        )
        self.assertIsNotNone(results)
        self.assertTrue(results["Foo.good"].exists)
        self.assertFalse(results["Foo.good"].sorry)
        self.assertTrue(results["Foo.bad"].exists)
        self.assertTrue(results["Foo.bad"].sorry)
        self.assertFalse(results["Foo.missing"].exists)

class LeanokPlacementClassificationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Statement-level \\leanok must downgrade sorry findings to a warning.

    Proof-level \\leanok keeps today's fail-safe behavior (hard error on
    ``sorryAx``), matching the decision recorded in docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md.
    """

    def test_decl_leanok_placement_picks_strongest_marker(self) -> None:
        def mk(statement: bool, proof: bool) -> BlueprintEntry:
            return BlueprintEntry(
                file="ch.tex",
                line=1,
                env_type="theorem",
                label=None,
                lean_decl="Foo.bar",
                has_leanok=statement,
                proof_has_leanok=proof,
            )

        # A decl with both statement-level and proof-level entries is
        # classified by the strongest placement seen across entries.
        self.assertEqual(_decl_leanok_placement([mk(True, False)]), "statement")
        self.assertEqual(_decl_leanok_placement([mk(True, True)]), "proof")
        self.assertEqual(_decl_leanok_placement([mk(False, True)]), "proof")
        self.assertEqual(_decl_leanok_placement([mk(False, False)]), "none")
        self.assertEqual(
            _decl_leanok_placement([mk(True, False), mk(False, True)]),
            "proof",
        )

    def _run_audit_with_axioms(
        self,
        entries: list[BlueprintEntry],
        *,
        axioms_by_decl: dict[str, list[str]],
    ):
        """Drive ``audit_blueprint`` without touching Lean or the filesystem.

        Patches the blueprint/Lean source collection and the axiom harness
        so the test can focus on the placement-aware classification logic.
        """
        fake_lean_decls = {
            entry.lean_decl: LeanDecl(
                file="MIPStarRE/Fake.lean",
                line=1,
                fqn=entry.lean_decl,
                kind="theorem",
                short_name=entry.lean_decl.split(".")[-1],
                end_line=1,
            )
            for entry in entries
        }

        def fake_axiom_checks(decls, **_kwargs):
            return {
                decl: DeclAxiomInfo(exists=True, axioms=list(axioms_by_decl.get(decl, [])))
                for decl in decls
            }

        # ``audit_blueprint`` is chatty — its progress lines would spam the
        # test runner's output and drown out real failures. Suppress stdout
        # so only assertion failures break the silence.
        with (
            mock.patch(
                "blueprint_leanok_axioms.collect_blueprint_entries",
                return_value=entries,
            ),
            mock.patch(
                "blueprint_leanok_axioms.collect_lean_decls",
                return_value=fake_lean_decls,
            ),
            mock.patch(
                "blueprint_leanok_axioms.run_decl_axiom_checks",
                side_effect=fake_axiom_checks,
            ),
            contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()),
        ):
            return audit_blueprint(
                Path("/tmp/fake-repo"),
                lake="lake",
                check_axioms=True,
                warn_missing_leanok=False,
            )

    def _entry(
        self,
        decl: str,
        *,
        has_leanok: bool,
        proof_has_leanok: bool,
    ) -> BlueprintEntry:
        return BlueprintEntry(
            file="src/chapter/ch_test.tex",
            line=1,
            env_type="theorem",
            label=None,
            lean_decl=decl,
            has_leanok=has_leanok,
            proof_has_leanok=proof_has_leanok,
        )

    def test_proof_level_leanok_with_sorry_is_hard_failure(self) -> None:
        entries = [self._entry("Foo.proof", has_leanok=True, proof_has_leanok=True)]
        result = self._run_audit_with_axioms(
            entries,
            axioms_by_decl={"Foo.proof": ["Classical.choice", "sorryAx"]},
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(result.failures), 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.failures[0].placement, "proof")
        self.assertEqual(result.warnings, [])

    def test_statement_only_leanok_with_sorry_is_warning_not_error(self) -> None:
        entries = [self._entry("Foo.stmt", has_leanok=True, proof_has_leanok=False)]
        result = self._run_audit_with_axioms(
            entries,
            axioms_by_decl={"Foo.stmt": ["sorryAx"]},
        )
        # Statement-level only must never hard-fail: the blueprint entry does
        # not claim proof completeness, so downgrade to a warning.
        self.assertEqual(result.failures, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(result.warnings), 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.warnings[0].placement, "statement")
        self.assertIn("statement-level", result.warnings[0].reason)

    def test_proof_level_sorry_free_still_passes(self) -> None:
        entries = [self._entry("Foo.ok", has_leanok=True, proof_has_leanok=True)]
        result = self._run_audit_with_axioms(
            entries,
            axioms_by_decl={"Foo.ok": ["Classical.choice"]},
        )
        self.assertEqual(result.failures, [])
        self.assertEqual(result.warnings, [])
        self.assertEqual(result.pass_count, 1)

            "scripts/tests/test_check_blueprint_latex.py",
        },
        "workflows": {".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml"},
    },
}

WORKFLOW_REQUIRED_PATHS = {
    ".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml": {
        "blueprint/**",
        "scripts/**",
        ".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml",
    },
}

_PATHS_KEY_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<indent>\s*)(?:paths|'paths'|\"paths\"):\s*"
    r"(?:(?P<anchor>&[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\s*)?"
    r"(?:(?P<alias>\*[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)|(?P<flow>\[[^\n]*\]))?"
    r"\s*(?:#.*)?$"
)
_PATH_ENTRY_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<indent>\s*)-\s+"
    r"(?P<scalar>(?:'[^'\n]*'|\"[^\"\n]*\"|[^#\n]*?))"
    r"(?:\s+#.*)?\s*$"
)
_ON_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<indent>\s*)(?:on|'on'|\"on\"):\s*(?:#.*)?$")
_YAML_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<indent>\s*)[^:#]+:\s*.*$")


def _unquote_path_scalar(scalar: str) -> str:
    scalar = scalar.strip()
    if len(scalar) >= 2 and scalar[0] == scalar[-1] and scalar[0] in {"'", '"'}:
        return scalar[1:-1]
    return scalar


def _flow_path_scalars(flow: str) -> set[str]:
    """Parse a simple YAML flow-style path list such as ``['a', \"b\"]``."""

    entries: list[str] = []
    current: list[str] = []
    quote: str | None = None
    for char in flow.strip()[1:-1]:
        if quote is not None:
            current.append(char)
            if char == quote:
                quote = None
        elif char in {"'", '"'}:
            quote = char
            current.append(char)
        elif char == ",":
            entries.append("".join(current))
            current = []
        else:
            current.append(char)
    entries.append("".join(current))

    return {
        path
        for entry in entries
        if (path := _unquote_path_scalar(entry))
    }


def path_filter_blocks(text: str) -> list[set[str]]:
    """Extract entries from GitHub Actions trigger ``paths:`` filters."""

    blocks: list[set[str]] = []
    anchors: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    in_on = False
    on_indent = 0
    event_indent: int | None = None
    event_child_indent: int | None = None
    in_paths = False
    paths_indent = 0
    current_block: set[str] = set()
    current_anchor: str | None = None

    def finish_current_block() -> None:
        nonlocal current_anchor, current_block, in_paths
        block = set(current_block)
        blocks.append(block)
        if current_anchor is not None:
            anchors[current_anchor] = block
        current_anchor = None
        current_block = set()
        in_paths = False

    def start_paths_block(match: re.Match[str]) -> None:
        nonlocal current_anchor, current_block, in_paths, paths_indent
        anchor = match.group("anchor")
        anchor_name = anchor.removeprefix("&") if anchor else None
        if alias := match.group("alias"):
            blocks.append(set(anchors.get(alias.removeprefix("*"), set())))
        elif flow := match.group("flow"):
            block = _flow_path_scalars(flow)
            blocks.append(block)
            if anchor_name is not None:
                anchors[anchor_name] = block
        else:
            in_paths = True
            paths_indent = len(match.group("indent"))
            current_block = set()
            current_anchor = anchor_name

    for raw_line in text.splitlines():
        while True:
            stripped = raw_line.strip()
            if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
                break
            indent = len(raw_line) - len(raw_line.lstrip(" "))

            if in_paths:
                if indent <= paths_indent:
                    finish_current_block()
                    # Reconsider this same line: it might start another paths block.
                    continue
                if match := _PATH_ENTRY_RE.match(raw_line):
                    path = _unquote_path_scalar(match.group("scalar"))
                    if path:
                        current_block.add(path)
                break

            if in_on:
                if indent <= on_indent:
                    in_on = False
                    event_indent = None
                    event_child_indent = None
                    # Reconsider this same line: it might start another top-level block.
                    continue

                if match := _PATHS_KEY_RE.match(raw_line):
                    path_key_indent = len(match.group("indent"))
                    if event_indent is not None and (
                        event_child_indent is None or path_key_indent == event_child_indent
                    ):
                        event_child_indent = path_key_indent
                        start_paths_block(match)
                    break

                if match := _YAML_KEY_RE.match(raw_line):
                    key_indent = len(match.group("indent"))
                    if event_indent is None or key_indent <= event_indent:
                        event_indent = key_indent
                        event_child_indent = None
                    elif event_child_indent is None:
                        event_child_indent = key_indent
                break

            if match := _ON_KEY_RE.match(raw_line):
                in_on = True
                on_indent = len(match.group("indent"))
                event_indent = None
                event_child_indent = None
            break

    if in_paths:
        finish_current_block()
    return blocks

    """Extract path-filter blocks from a GitHub Actions workflow file."""

    return path_filter_blocks((PROJECT_ROOT / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Smoke tests for scripts/make_artifact.sh.

The script is driven against a throwaway git repository built in a temporary
directory, so these tests are fast, offline, and independent of the state of
the real repository. What they pin down is the behaviour a release depends on:
the allow-list actually excludes the workflow layer, the leak scan actually
fails the run, and `--anonymize` actually rewrites.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import tarfile
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "make_artifact.sh"

LEAN_MAIN = """import MIPStarRE.Bar

/-- A doc comment: this line does not count as code.
    Neither does this one. -/
theorem foo : True := trivial
"""

LEAN_BAR = "theorem bar : True := trivial\n"


def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    """Run git in *repo* with a fixed identity, returning stripped stdout."""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(repo), "-c", "user.name=Test", "-c", "user.email=test@example.invalid",
         "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", *args],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    )
    return proc.stdout.strip()


def write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def minimal_pdf(text: str) -> bytes:
    """A one-page PDF whose only visible content is *text*, built by hand.

    Short enough to keep in the test, and real enough that pdftotext reads it.
    Its job is to put a binary into the snapshot: the leak scan skips binaries
    by construction, so a PDF is the one shipped file that could otherwise
    carry a home path past it.

    The header carries the binary-marker comment that real PDF writers emit,
    with a NUL byte in it, and that byte is what makes this a binary at all: a
    hand-built PDF is otherwise plain ASCII, which the script would classify as
    text and happily rewrite in place, so a test built on one would exercise
    the text path and prove nothing about binaries. A comment is ignored by
    every reader, so the file stays valid.
    """
    stream = ("BT /F1 12 Tf 20 100 Td (%s) Tj ET" % text).encode("ascii")
    objects = [
        b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
        b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
        b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 300 200]"
        b" /Resources << /Font << /F1 5 0 R >> >> /Contents 4 0 R >>",
        b"<< /Length %d >>\nstream\n%s\nendstream" % (len(stream), stream),
        b"<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>",
    ]
    out = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.4\n%\xe2\xe3\xcf\xd3\x00\n")
    offsets = []
    for number, body in enumerate(objects, start=1):
        offsets.append(len(out))
        out += b"%d 0 obj\n" % number + body + b"\nendobj\n"
    xref = len(out)
    out += b"xref\n0 %d\n" % (len(objects) + 1)
    out += b"0000000000 65535 f \n"
    for offset in offsets:
        out += b"%010d 00000 n \n" % offset
    out += b"trailer\n<< /Size %d /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % (
        len(objects) + 1, xref)
    return bytes(out)


class MakeArtifactTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Each test gets its own repository; they mutate it freely."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.tmp = Path(self._tmp.name)
        self.addCleanup(self._tmp.cleanup)
        self.repo = self.tmp / "repo"
        self.out = self.tmp / "out"
        self.repo.mkdir()
        git(self.repo, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")

        write(self.repo / "MIPStarRE.lean", "import MIPStarRE.Foo\n")
        write(self.repo / "MIPStarRE" / "Foo.lean", LEAN_MAIN)
        write(self.repo / "MIPStarRE" / "Bar.lean", LEAN_BAR)
        write(self.repo / "lean-toolchain", "leanprover/lean4:v4.32.0\n")
        write(self.repo / "lakefile.toml", 'name = "MIPStarRE"\n')
        write(self.repo / "lake-manifest.json", json.dumps(
            {"packages": [{"name": "mathlib", "rev": "deadbeefcafe"}]}))
        write(self.repo / "README.md", "See https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A\n")
        write(self.repo / "docs" / "comparator.md", "trust model\n")
        # Third-party paper sources: they ship (owner decision, 2026-09-19).
        write(self.repo / "references" / "qpbt-paper" / "frontmatter.tex",
              "\\title{A paper}\n")
        # The workflow layer: excluded by the allow-list, and carrying exactly
        # the kind of home path the leak scan exists to catch.
        write(self.repo / "local" / "bin" / "tool.sh", "cd /home/somebody/checkout\n")
        write(self.repo / "results" / "telemetry" / "builds.jsonl", '{"ok":true}\n')
        self.commit()

    def commit(self, message: str = "test") -> str:
        git(self.repo, "add", "-A")
        git(self.repo, "commit", "-q", "--no-verify", "-m", message)
        return git(self.repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")

    def run_script(self, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        # Start from an empty output directory every time.  A test that runs the
        # script twice commits in between, so the second run writes a tarball and
        # a MANIFEST under a *different* commit-derived name beside the first
        # ones; `self.out.glob(...)` then returns them in an unspecified order
        # and an assertion about the second run may read the first run's file.
        shutil.rmtree(self.out, ignore_errors=True)
        return subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(SCRIPT), *args, "HEAD", str(self.out)],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
            env={"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin", "HOME": str(self.tmp),
                 "MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT": str(self.repo)},
        )

    def install_packaging_script(self, suffix: str = "") -> Path:
        """Install the real packaging script in the fixture repository."""
        shipped = self.repo / "scripts" / "make_artifact.sh"
        write(shipped, SCRIPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + suffix)
        return shipped

    def members(self) -> list[str]:
        """Snapshot-relative paths inside the one tarball in the out directory."""
        tarballs = sorted(self.out.glob("*.tar.gz"))
        self.assertEqual(len(tarballs), 1, f"expected one tarball, got {tarballs}")
        with tarfile.open(tarballs[0]) as archive:
            return [name.split("/", 1)[1] for name in archive.getnames() if "/" in name]

    # -- what ships ---------------------------------------------------------

    def test_packages_the_development_and_drops_the_workflow_layer(self) -> None:
        head = git(self.repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
        result = self.run_script()
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        names = self.members()
        for shipped in ("MIPStarRE/Foo.lean", "MIPStarRE/Bar.lean", "MIPStarRE.lean",
                        "lean-toolchain", "README.md", "MANIFEST.txt"):
            self.assertIn(shipped, names)
        for excluded in ("local/bin/tool.sh", "results/telemetry/builds.jsonl"):
            self.assertNotIn(excluded, names)
        self.assertIn(head, result.stdout)
        self.assertIn("sha256", result.stdout)

    def test_the_paper_sources_ship(self) -> None:
        """They are what the docstring `file.tex:lines` locators point at."""
        self.assertEqual(self.run_script().returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("references/qpbt-paper/frontmatter.tex", self.members())

    def test_manifest_records_toolchain_mathlib_and_lean_code_lines(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(self.run_script().returncode, 0)
        manifest = next(self.out.glob("*.MANIFEST.txt")).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn("leanprover/lean4:v4.32.0", manifest)
        self.assertIn("deadbeefcafe", manifest)
        self.assertIn("Lean files        : 3", manifest)
        # Foo.lean: import + theorem are code, the two doc-comment lines and the
        # blank lines are not; Bar.lean and MIPStarRE.lean are one line each.
        self.assertIn("Lean code lines   : 4 ", manifest)

    def test_reports_an_import_that_is_not_in_the_snapshot(self) -> None:
        (self.repo / "MIPStarRE" / "Bar.lean").unlink()

        manifest = next(self.out.glob("*.MANIFEST.txt")).read_text(encoding="utf-8")

# Makefile for the paper-gap notes.
#
# Each note in this directory is a standalone LaTeX document that justifies one
# correction made to a source-paper statement during formalization.  They are
# the reviewer-facing half of the qpbt-gap-register.md summary table, so a
# reviewer must be able to build them with a stock TeX installation and nothing
# else.  This Makefile is that path: plain latexmk, no external tooling.
#
#   make          compile every note into build/ (also `make all`)
#   make check    compile, then fail on any LaTeX error, undefined reference,
#                 undefined citation or multiply-defined label
#   make pages    print the page count of every built note
#   make clean    remove build/
#
# The repository's own CI runs `texra-blueprint --root . paper-gaps check`
# (local/bin/ci.sh, step `paper-gaps`), which validates cross-note slugs and
# registered source keys.  That check and this Makefile are complementary: the
# CI step needs texra-blueprint, this one does not.
#
# build/ is ignored (see the repository .gitignore); no PDF is committed.  The
# artifact packaging step builds the PDFs at release time.

LATEXMK      ?= latexmk
BUILDDIR     := build
LATEXMKFLAGS := -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -file-line-error \
                -output-directory=$(BUILDDIR)

# Every .tex in this directory that is a document in its own right.  command.tex
# is a macro file included by the notes and must not be compiled on its own.
NOTES := $(shell grep -l '^[[:space:]]*\\documentclass' *.tex 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)
PDFS  := $(NOTES:%.tex=$(BUILDDIR)/%.pdf)

.PHONY: all check clean list pages
.DELETE_ON_ERROR:

all: $(PDFS)

$(BUILDDIR):
	@mkdir -p $(BUILDDIR)

$(BUILDDIR)/%.pdf: %.tex command.tex references.bib | $(BUILDDIR)
	$(LATEXMK) $(LATEXMKFLAGS) $<

list:
	@for n in $(NOTES); do echo "$$n"; done

pages: all
	@for n in $(NOTES); do \
	  pdf=$(BUILDDIR)/$${n%.tex}.pdf; \
	  if command -v pdfinfo >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    p=$$(pdfinfo "$$pdf" 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Pages:/ {print $$2}'); \
	  else \
	    p=$$(grep -c '/Type[[:space:]]*/Page[^s]' "$$pdf" 2>/dev/null); \
	  fi; \
	  printf '%-60s %s\n' "$$n" "$${p:-?}"; \
	done

# A LaTeX error already fails `all`, because -halt-on-error makes latexmk exit
# non-zero.  What latexmk does NOT fail on is an unresolved \ref or \cite or a
# duplicated label, so scan the logs for those.  Anchoring on the warning
# prefix rather than on the word "undefined" keeps the match reliable: LaTeX
# wraps log lines at 79 columns, and it emits "LaTeX Warning: Reference ..." /
# "LaTeX Warning: Citation ..." only when the key is unresolved.
check: all
	@status=0; \
	for n in $(NOTES); do \
	  base=$${n%.tex}; log=$(BUILDDIR)/$$base.log; pdf=$(BUILDDIR)/$$base.pdf; \
	  if [ ! -s "$$pdf" ]; then \
	    echo "ERROR: $$n produced no PDF"; status=1; \
	  fi; \
	  if [ ! -f "$$log" ]; then \
	    echo "ERROR: $$n produced no log"; status=1; continue; \
	  fi; \
	  bad=$$(grep -E '^LaTeX Warning: (Reference|Citation) |undefined references|multiply defined|^! |^Emergency stop|^Fatal error' "$$log" || true); \
	  if [ -n "$$bad" ]; then \
	    echo "ERROR: $$n"; printf '%s\n' "$$bad" | sed 's/^/    /'; status=1; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	if [ $$status -ne 0 ]; then \
	  echo "paper-gaps check: FAILED"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	echo "paper-gaps check: $(words $(NOTES)) notes built, no LaTeX errors, no undefined references"

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILDDIR)
